effect_estimate.comment: All independent variables were natural-log transformed; Models 1 and 3 used GLM with a logit link for municipal share of households with piped water (bounded between 0 and 1), and Model 2 used OLS for log cumulative per capita federal transfers in constant 2002 pesos.
effect_estimate.value: Higher municipal indigenous population share in 2000 significantly predicted lower piped water coverage in 2005 in GLM logit-link regression (b = -0.0310, robust SE = 0.0126, z = -2.4500, p = 0.0140, N = 2,372) controlling for 2000 baseline water coverage, density, income, migration, spatial lag, and state dummies. In OLS regression of log cumulative per capita federal transfers (Aportaciones Federales, 2000-2005; N = 2,342, adjusted R2 = 0.72), indigenous share was negatively associated with transfers (b = -0.003, SE = 0.001, t = -2.800, p = 0.005; a 1% increase in indigenous share reduced federal transfers by 0.01 percentage points), whereas 2000 presidential winning-party vote share increased transfers (b = 0.063, SE = 0.019, t = 3.340, p = 0.001) and 2000 baseline water coverage also increased transfers (b = 0.009, SE = 0.003, t = 3.520, p = 0.000). Adding per capita transfers to the 2005 water coverage GLM (N = 2,342) showed a positive effect of federal transfers on piped water coverage (b = 0.5713, robust SE = 0.2437, z = 2.3400, p = 0.0190), while the negative indigenous share coefficient attenuated slightly to b = -0.0305 (robust SE = 0.0127, z = -2.4000, p = 0.0170).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling for observational JBI cross-sectional regression is 2; rated 1 (documented association) because the study tests statistical associations using aggregate municipal census data and multi-sector federal transfers (Aportaciones Federales, which aggregate infrastructure, health, education, and other programmes) rather than directly observing administrative allocation rules or agency practices, and notes that further study is needed to identify remaining mechanisms.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 8-12, Unit of analysis, data and methodology, Results, and Conclusion; Tables 3-5

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines intergovernmental fiscal transfers (Aportaciones Federales) and presidential partisan/clientelist alignment (political_coordination), systematic under-allocation of federal transfers to indigenous municipalities (discretion), constitutional decentralisation to municipalities under Article 115 paired with weak local fiscal/administrative capacity and reliance on federal transfers (institutional_fragmentation), and government spatial infrastructure investment planning prioritising dense urban areas over dispersed rural settlements (planning).

study_design.comment: Combines 1999 economic census, 2000 population census, 2005 population survey, and 2000-2005 municipal public finance data from INEGI across three municipal-level regression specifications (GLM with logit link for 2005 piped water coverage in Models 1 and 3, and OLS for cumulative per capita federal transfers in Model 2) controlling for 2000 baseline piped water coverage, population density, per capita income, international migration, presidential vote share, queen-contiguity spatial lag, and state dummy variables.
study_design.value: Observational municipal-level regression analysis (generalised linear models with logit link and ordinary least squares with spatial lag and state dummy variables)
